verses.141:4b: Neste caminho por onde eu andava, * {laqueum}.
verses.141:5: {considerabam} à direita, e via: * e não havia quem me conhecesse.
verses.141:5b: A fuga {periit}, * e não há quem {requirat} a minha alma.

decisions.latin: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: voce mea ad Dóminum deprecátus sum
decisions.why: The first colon is word for word 3:5a and 76:2a, both already Com a minha voz clamei ao Senhor (concord.py) — identical Latin, identical Portuguese (rule 6). The second colon keeps the Latin's repetition (voz, ao Senhor) and deprecári → suplicar (D35). The whole verse is also sung alone as the Introit psalm verse of the Stigmata of St Francis (missa Sancti/09-17), so it must stand without context — it does. The CNBB (fetched, circulation.md) and a Protestant hymn have the present (imploro / clamo … suplico); the Latin has two perfects, and 129:1 kept the perfect against the familiar present clamo the same way.

options.label: clamei … supliquei
options.note: draft — the Latin's perfects; 3:5a, 76:2a

options.label: clamo … suplico
options.note: the present, as the CNBB Liturgia das Horas and the HCC hymn (from the Hebrew's imperfects); breaks the doublet with 3:5a and 76:2a

decisions.why: The conspéctus row splits: à vista de where the phrase is a predicate or the place of witnesses, na … presença beside an act of worship (17:7b, 21:28b, 49:3b, 99:2b, 137:1b) and with third-person pronouns, where à vista dele was heard badly (79:10). Pouring out a prayer is an act of worship. Na sua presença is also exactly the CNBB's wording (fetched). It stays apart from ante ipsum → diante dele in the next colon, as the Latin has two phrases. Draft 2 moves the phrase after the object (Derramo a minha oração na sua presença), the stylist's order: the two colons no longer both end on a minha …ção. Order only (D2).

options.label: na sua presença
options.note: draft — the row's worship sense; MS1932 na sua presença

options.label: à vista dele
options.note: the row's other rendering, keeps the noun of seeing; 79:10 found à vista dele heard badly

decisions.why: pronuntiáre (ἀπαγγελῶ, 'report, declare') has an open row, pronunciar (118:13, 118:172, 70:17), whose stylist already found it technical. Pronuncio a minha tribulação is heard as uttering a word or a sentence (a judge pronounces). Declaro is the plain Portuguese of saying something out openly and is DRB's 'declare'; exponho (MS1932, and the HCC hymn) is expónere, another Latin image (setting out). Ruled declaro; the row is left open, with this place recorded. The Latin's object-first order is not kept: it would put the verb at the cadence (e a minha tribulação diante dele declaro) in a verb-final order Portuguese uses only for effect; ending on tribulação keeps the noun at the cadence as the Latin ends on its verb.

options.label: declaro
options.note: draft — DRB 'declare'

options.label: pronuncio
options.note: the open row's cognate (118:13, 172; 70:17)

options.label: exponho
options.note: MS1932; natural in Brazilian prayer, but another Latin verb's image

decisions.latin: In deficiéndo ex me spíritum meum
decisions.why: A gerund with an accusative subject, ἐν τῷ ἐκλείπειν ἐξ ἐμοῦ τὸ πνεῦμά μου: 'in my spirit's failing out of me'. Portuguese needs a clause. ex me is 'from / out of me' — the spirit failing and going out; em mim keeps the person without the motion, de mim after desfalecer would be heard as cause ('fainting from me'). desfalecer is the verb 76:4 already has for defécit spíritus meus; the CNBB has Quando em mim desfalece a minh'alma (fetched). The order puts em mim at the mediant so the colon does not end on the proparoxytone espírito (rule 4). The v2 Latinist (minor) asked desfalecia de mim for ex me. Held: desfalecer de is heard as the cause of fainting, which is a wrong first hearing; the motion of ex me is offered by option 1 (se esvaía de mim), which changes the verb. The ambiguity reader heard em mim without trouble.

options.label: Quando o meu espírito desfalecia em mim

forms.deficiendo: Quando o meu espírito desfalecia em mim

options.note: draft

options.label: Quando o meu espírito se esvaía de mim

options.note: keeps the motion of ex me, but another verb than 76:4's desfalecer

options.label: Quando o meu espírito me desfalecia

forms.deficiendo: Quando o meu espírito me desfalecia

options.note: a dative of the person, DRB's 'failed me'; desfalecer does not usually take one

options.label: Quando o meu espírito desfalecia de mim

forms.deficiendo: Quando o meu espírito desfalecia de mim

options.note: the v2 Latinist's fix, ex me as de mim; after desfalecer, de is heard as cause (desfalecer de fome) or not at all

decisions.why: The et opens the main clause after the temporal gerund — the Hebrew-and-Greek 'and' of the apodosis (καὶ σύ), which DRB turns to 'then' and MS1932 drops. In Portuguese quando …, e vós conhecestes reads as a broken sentence. The emphatic tu is kept as vós named; only the conjunction goes, as grammar (D2). The Latinist (v1, minor, his only remark) asked for the et back. Refused: after quando the Portuguese e opens nothing — it would be heard as a second temporal clause left without a main verb; MS1932 drops it too. The emphatic tu stays as vós named. Kept as option 1. The v2 Latinist (minor) proposed então vós. Held: então makes the knowing follow the fainting in time ("only then you knew"), a reading the Latin does not force — it can as well be "you knew all along"; the bare vós leaves that open, and DRB's then is a choice among them.

options.label: vós
options.note: draft — MS1932 also drops the et (tu conheceste)

options.label: e vós
options.note: the Latin's et kept

options.label: então vós
options.note: DRB 'then thou knewest' — the sense of the apodotic et made a word; asked by the v2 Latinist (minor)

decisions.why: abscóndere → esconder and láqueus → laço (63:6b esconderiam laços). The dative mihi is the one the snare is aimed at. Para mim says that and is DRB's 'for me'; esconderam-me um laço can be heard as 'hid a snare from me' (a true but different sense). MS1932 armaram-me laços ocultos changes the verb (láqueum pónere is armar / pôr, 118:110). The CNBB has contra mim ocultaram ciladas. In via hac: neste caminho keeps the demonstrative. Ruled in draft 2 for the clitic (stylist): it is grammar, not a word, and the reading 'hid it from me' that made draft 1 avoid it is a true sense of a hidden snare, not a wrong one.

options.label: esconderam-me um laço
options.note: draft 2 — the stylist's: the clitic is what the prayed register expects; the dative is as open as the Latin mihi (aimed at me / hidden from me)

options.label: esconderam um laço para mim
options.note: draft 1 — DRB 'hidden a snare for me'

options.label: esconderam um laço contra mim
options.note: names the hostility the dative implies (CNBB's contra mim)

decisions.why: consideráre (κατενόουν, looked closely) has the row: considerar for things, observar with a person (21:18) and in absolute use (93:9 não observa). Here it is absolute, with ad déxteram — the side where a defender or witness stood. Eu is supplied because observava is also 'he observed'. à direita: déxtera → a direita (row), with no possessive, as the Latin (MS1932 and DRB add 'my'). Two imperfects kept.

options.label: Eu observava
options.note: draft — the row's absolute use (93:9)

options.label: Olhava
options.note: plainer; but olhar is the plain seeing verb, and vidébam follows; the stylist's proposal (Olhava à direita), refused: olhar is the plain verb of looking, κατενόουν is looking closely, and the row gives observar for the absolute use (93:9). The pronoun is kept because olhava / observava is also 'he'.

options.label: Eu considerava
options.note: the cognate; heard as 'I was pondering'

decisions.why: períre → perecer (working row), but the row already names the other sense: 118:176 ovis quæ périit → se perdeu, because perecer is only 'die'. Flight (the way of escape) is not a thing that dies; it is lost to someone — ἀπώλετο φυγὴ ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ, the same Greek verb as 118:176. Perdeu-se para mim a fuga keeps the verb's sense, the noun, and a me as para mim; de mim would make a fuga de mim 'flight from me'. DRB 'Flight hath failed me'; MS1932 paraphrases (Não me ficou possibilidade de fuga). Draft 1 had Perdeu-se para mim a fuga (the Latin's order); the stylist called it the worst line (the subject dangles) and the ambiguity reader found it hard to parse, so draft 2 puts the subject first. The stylist's Não há mais fuga para mim was refused: it drops the verb (périit) and makes a statement of existence out of an event; it would also make the verse say não há twice where the Latin has périit … non est.

options.label: se perdeu para mim
options.note: draft 2 — the subject first (stylist and ambiguity reader both stumbled on the inversion of draft 1); the verb kept

options.label: pereceu para mim
options.note: the row's working verb (9:7b Pereceu a memória deles)

options.label: foi-se de mim
options.note: plain, keeps 'from me' as de mim; loses the sense of loss

options.label: não existe mais para mim
options.note: the stylist's sense (Não há mais fuga para mim) in the slot; drops périit

decisions.why: requírere → procurar (row; ἐκζητῶν). Here the seeking is a friend's care ('no one looks for me'), where elsewhere quǽrere ánimam is the enemies' hunt for a life (53:5 → buscar). procurar keeps requírere apart from quǽrere and ánima → a minha alma (row). Whether the ear hears care or hostility is for the ambiguity reader; MS1932 (se importe com a minha vida) and the CNBB (não importa a ninguém minha vida) turn it into care outright, which interprets.

options.label: procure
options.note: draft — the row

options.label: se importe com
options.note: MS1932's sense, plain; interprets the verb

decisions.why: custódia is a guard, a watch, a prison; here φυλακή as the place one is brought out of — DRB 'prison', MS1932 desta prisão, the CNBB da prisão. The rows so far (38:2b guarda; 89:5, 129:6 vigília) are the other senses; this adds prisão for the place. edúcere de with a source → tirar de (row: 29:4, 30:5, 39:3). The colon is also the Thursday Vespers antiphon (Educ de custódia * ánimam meam, Dómine, ad confiténdum nómini tuo), and stands alone.

options.label: prisão
options.note: draft — DRB, MS1932

options.label: cárcere
options.note: same sense, more solemn, proparoxytone

decisions.why: exspectáre → aguardar (D39). The Latin puts me first and the subject last; os justos me aguardam is the plain order. The Latin's present is kept (the Greek has a future, ὑπομενοῦσιν; the Hebrew 'will surround me', which the CNBB follows — not taken).

options.label: os justos me aguardam
options.note: draft

options.label: aguardam-me os justos
options.note: the Latin's order, subject last

decisions.why: retribúere → retribuir (115:3, 137:8, 17:21); the open row makes Recompensai only for the vós imperative (118:17), where retribuí collides with the past. The stylist found retribuais bookish at the cadence and asked recompenseis; the ambiguity reader listed retribuais as unknown. Refused: the subjunctive has no collision, and the family retribuir / retribuição is kept across the psalter (the row). Recompensar also decides for reward, where the Latin (and the ambiguity reader) hear repayment either way.

options.label: me retribuais
options.note: draft — the row

options.label: me recompenseis
options.note: the stylist's; 118:17's imperative verb; decides for reward

decisions.why: The colon is word for word 17:18b (quóniam confortáti sunt super me → porque se fortaleceram mais do que eu), so identical Latin keeps identical Portuguese (rule 6). ὑπὲρ ἐμέ is comparative in Greek usage (DRB and MS1932: stronger than I); in Ps 17 the stylist heard acima de mim as a place, and the comparison was taken. The v2 Latinist (minor) asks sobre mim to keep the Latin open between "beyond me" and "over / against me". Held for the doublet; sobre mim is an option and, if taken, should be taken in 17:18 too.

options.label: se fortaleceram mais do que eu

forms.super_me: se fortaleceram mais do que eu

options.label: se fortaleceram sobre mim
options.note: the v2 Latinist's; keeps super open; would break the doublet with 17:18b

choices.141:2: No title: DO's Latin file starts at 141:2 and has no titulus (D7); the Vulgate title Intellectus David, cum esset in spelunca, oratio is not translated. The whole verse is the Introit psalm verse of 09-17.
choices.141:4b: via → caminho, ambuláre → andar (rows); eu supplied because andava is also 'he walked'.
choices.141:5: cognóscere → conhecer (row); the imperfect subjunctive conhecesse as MS1932.
choices.141:6: Clamei a vós as 118:146; eu disse as 118:57, whose Pórtio mea is also a porção; terra vivéntium → terra dos vivos (26:13, 51:7). The monastic Vespers antiphon Pórtio mea, Dómine, sit in terra vivéntium is built from this colon. The second colon is long (the Latin's is 19 syllables); accepted. The stylist asked e disse and minha porção without the article, for breath: refused — the article before possessives is a style rule, and e supplies a conjunction the Latin lacks (the same reason the apodotic et of 141:4 is not supplied); eu disse as 118:57.
choices.141:7: inténde → atendei (D3), deprecátio → prece (D35); humiliátus sum nimis → fui humilhado sem medida, as 37:9 and 115:1. The ambiguity reader heard humilhado as 'shamed' first, 'brought low' second; the row is shared with 37:9 and 115:1, kept.
choices.141:7b: The second colon is 17:18's word for word (porque se fortaleceram mais do que eu, super me as a comparison). liberáre → livrar (row).
choices.141:8: ad confiténdum nómini tuo → para dar graças ao vosso nome (D5; 121:4's build). retribúere → retribuir; retribuais is the subjunctive, not the imperative the open row is about.
choices.141:4: The ambiguity reader listed veredas and desfalecia as unknown: both are rows (sémita → vereda, D15, often reported unknown and kept; desfalecer, 76:4) and kept.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932; pt-PT looked at only as the text to be replaced; no DM1962 for this psalm). Title checked in DO's file: absent, so none (D7). Precedent by concord.py: 3:5a = 76:2a for the first colon; 17:18, 37:9, 115:1, 118:57, 118:146, 121:4. Liturgical use by grep and the CNBB Liturgia das Horas fetched: circulation.md. Hard readings: the gerund in deficiéndo ex me with the apodotic et, périit fuga a me (perecer or the 'lost' sense of 118:176), pronuntiáre (open row), consideráre absolute.

Hard checks pass. Soft, all accepted: 141:4 first colon +3 and 141:4b first colon +3 by the non-eliding counter (o‿meu, desfalecia‿em, onde‿eu: about +1 said); 141:6 second colon +4 (the Latin's colon is already the longest, 19; the list of predicates is the Latin's); 141:7 first colon −4 (deprecatiónem is one long word; prece was chosen short on purpose, D35). Rhyme 141:2 Senhor / Senhor: the Latin's own repeated ad Dóminum, one word twice, not a rhyme to fix; the order follows 3:5a / 76:2a. Rhyme 141:3 oração / tribulação: the Latin has the same echo in its two parallel nouns (oratiónem meam / tribulatiónem meam); kept.
1 minor (141:4 the dropped et); refused, kept as an option. Overall: close and faithful.

outcomes.reason: After quando, Portuguese e opens no main clause and would be heard as a second dangling clause; conjunction is grammar (D2); MS1932 drops it.

audit.note: 6 remarks; 3 taken (141:3 order, 141:4b clitic, 141:5b order — the last partly: his order problem, not his wording), 3 refused and kept as options or choices. Best line 141:2, worst 141:5b.

audit.note: 15 ambiguities, 3 unknown words. Every likely hearing is the Latin's sense or one the Latin also leaves open (the prison literal/figurative, the just waiting, retribution as reward or repayment). 141:5b procure heard as care first — the test the requirat decision asked for; the hostile sense noted as possible, kept. 141:5b inversion hard to parse — mended by order. Unknown: veredas, desfalecia, retribuais — rows, kept.

outcomes.reason: Heard as care first, the sense; procurar is the row.
Shared with 37:9, 115:1; the Latin humiliátus holds both.

audit.note: v2: 141:3 na sua presença after the object (stylist, rhyme); 141:4b esconderam-me um laço (stylist); 141:5b A fuga se perdeu para mim (stylist + ambiguity, order). New decision retribuas records the refused recompenseis. prayed.v1.json kept. Checks re-run: hard pass; the 141:3 rhyme flag is gone; the other soft flags are those accepted in v1.
Gate on draft 2: no major. Three minors, all held with reasons and kept as options (no wording change): 141:4 ex me, 141:4 the apodotic et, 141:7b super me. Overall: faithful, close.
